subject: Post-call recap & pilot charter — observability use case for Solaris Systems
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tanguy <alex.tanguy@solaris-systems.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-31T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & pilot charter — observability use case for Solaris Systems

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. If anything below is off, flag it and we'll adjust.

Pain points you described:
- Increasing query latency and bursty costs for derived metrics during heavy ingest windows.
- Manual maintenance of prompt templates and lack of systematic evals for model regressions.
- Need for predictable per-query unit economics before production rollout.

Primary goals for the pilot:
1) Demonstrate stable p95 latency under realistic traffic (target: p95 < 300ms for small generation queries).
2) Show cost profile and estimate per-1k-token unit cost under our recommended batching and quantization settings (goal: < $0.60/1k effective tokens).
3) Build an initial prompt/eval suite (50 core prompts) that verifies functional correctness on the 3 top-priority workflows.

Proposed pilot scope (4 weeks):
- Week 0: access + baseline run (sample traffic, 1M tokens/day for 2 days).
- Week 1–2: integration, prompt set and eval scaffolding, perf runs for p95 measurements.
- Week 3: cost optimization pass (batching profiles, cache hints), run acceptance evals.
- Week 4: final report + handoff + optional extension discussion.

Success metrics (acceptance criteria):
- p95 latency < 300ms for defined small-gen workload (see attached charter).
- Quality benchmarks: >= 85% pass rate on the prompt/eval suite for primary workflows.
- Reproducible cost estimate and a recommended config for production.

Owners & immediate asks:
- Redwood technical owner: Karthik Iyer (will lead integration & perf runs).
- Redwood engagement owner: Jordan Blake (commercial/coordination).
- Solaris technical owner: Alex Tanguy (please confirm).

Access steps (high level) — we list the full checklist in the attachment:
- Solaris to provide a service account or temporary credentials for a test bucket + a sample dataset (top 3 queries).
- If you prefer VPC peering for data access, share network contact so our infra team can schedule the peer.

Attachments: pilot-charter-v1.pdf (scope, metrics, sample prompts)

Next steps: please confirm the Solaris technical owner and your procurement contact. If that looks good, Karthik and I will schedule a 30–45 minute kickoff for Tuesday Nov 3 to go through the access checklist and timeline.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]
[Attachment: pilot-charter-v1.pdf (PDF, 250KB)]

From: Alex Tanguy <alex.tanguy@solaris-systems.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, procurement@solaris-systems.com
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & pilot charter — observability use case for Solaris Systems

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few items from our side and adding constraints so the kickoff can be efficient.

Quick confirmations:
- Solaris technical owner: confirmed — that's me (Alex).
- Procurement contact: procurement@solaris-systems.com (I copied them). They will handle contract language and potential NDAs.

Constraints / notes:
- Compliance: any shared logs must be hashed and redacted; we can provide a scrubbed sample dataset by EOD Friday (Nov 5).
- Timeline: Nov 3 kickoff works for a 30-min call. Internal target: have procurement review basic SOW and sign off on sandbox access by Nov 10 so we can hit integrations the following week.

Two asks from Solaris before kickoff:
1) Karthik — can you confirm whether VPC peering is mandatory for the initial baseline runs or if a signed temporary bucket URL is sufficient?
2) Can you send a short list of the 50 core prompts planned for the eval (just titles & intent) so we can sanity-check them prior to the run?

Forwarding the pilot-charter to procurement now.

Best —
Alex
Alex Tanguy
Head of Data Products, Solaris Systems
[alex.tanguy@solaris-systems.com]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tanguy <alex.tanguy@solaris-systems.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & pilot charter — observability use case for Solaris Systems

Alex — quick technical notes and practical next steps. See attached access-checklist.xlsx for fields we need filled.

Short answers to your asks:
- VPC peering is preferred for production-like performance characterization, but for the initial baseline we can work with a pre-signed bucket URL and a scrubbed sample dataset. If you can provide VPC peering details later, we can swap to that mid-pilot.
- We'll circulate the draft prompt list (titles + intent) by end of day Nov 2 — Jordan will share the Drive link. Please flag any prompts that are not permitted on your side for compliance reasons.

Access checklist (high level):
- Provide a test GCS bucket (or S3) with read-only service account credentials OR a pre-signed URL with 7-day validity.
- Sample dataset: 2000 anonymized events across the 3 workloads (logs + associated metadata).
- Network: if opting for VPC peering, provide CIDR and contact for Solaris network team.
- API keys: Redwood will generate scoped keys for the pilot; we ask Solaris to whitelist Redwood IP range listed in the checklist.

Technical owners:
- Redwood runtime & perf: Karthik Iyer (karthik.iyer@redwood.ai)
- Redwood engagement & evaluation: Monica Patel (monica.patel@redwood.ai)

I'll join the Nov 3 kickoff and we can step through the checklist live.

[Attachment: access-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 40KB)]

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
